CM: Hi, good afternoon, this is Renata with Cadence care management. Am I speaking with, um, Joanne Pruitt?
DAUGHTER: Yes, this is Joanne. Is this about my dad?
CM: It is, it's about Harold. I saw a note that the hospice intake nurse came out to the house yesterday?
DAUGHTER: She did, she was here almost two hours. Her name was, uh, Bev, Beverly something, from Gentle Harbor Hospice.
CM: Okay good. So for the election paperwork I just need to confirm a couple things. Can you give me his date of birth?
DAUGHTER: November ninth, nineteen thirty-eight.
CM: Thank you. And his member ID, it's on the Cadence card.
DAUGHTER: Hang on, the card's in his wallet... okay it's C, D, four four seven, one nine oh two.
CM: C D four four seven one nine zero two. Perfect.
DAUGHTER: He's eighty-seven now and honestly the COPD has just, I mean he can't get to the bathroom without the oxygen anymore. He's on four liters.
CM: I'm so sorry. That's really what hospice is for. Has doctor Lindqvist signed the certification yet?
DAUGHTER: Doctor who? Oh, Lindqvist, his lung doctor. I think so, they said he faxed it Friday.
CM: Okay. And the address we have is forty-two eleven Sumner Road, is that still where he's staying?
DAUGHTER: No, no, that's the thing, he moved in with me back in August. I'm at nine eighteen Calloway Court, Bellbrook, four five three oh five.
CM: Got it. Is that Calloway with two L's?
DAUGHTER: Two L's, yep. C A L L O W A Y.
CM: And the best callback number for you?
DAUGHTER: My cell, nine three seven, five five five, zero one six two.
CM: Great. The hospice team usually starts visits within forty-eight hours of the signed election. They'll probably come Mondays and Thursdays to start, and the aide can help with baths.
DAUGHTER: Okay. Thank you, Renata, really. This has been a lot.
CM: Of course. Call me anytime, I'm here Monday through Friday.

CM: Okay, I think we're connected. Hi, this is Marcus Feld from Cadence, I have our member Priya Raman on the line with me.
DME: Hi, thanks for holding, this is Tonya in the pump department at Brightline Diabetic Supply. Can I get the patient's date of birth?
MEMBER: It's four, twelve, ninety-one.
DME: And the last name, sorry, was that Raman, R A M A N?
MEMBER: Yes. First name Priya, P R I Y A.
DME: Okay I see her. Last order shipped... July twenty-second, so she's due for infusion sets and reservoirs.
MEMBER: Right, I'm completely out of reservoirs as of, like, this morning. I've been stretching them.
CM: Is there a hold on the account? She said she got a letter.
DME: Yeah, there's a hold because we need a new prescription. The one from doctor Achebe expired on the thirtieth.
MEMBER: But I just saw her two weeks ago!
DME: She may not have sent it over. Happens a lot.
CM: I'll call Northgate Endocrine right after this. What's the account number so they can reference it?
DME: Account is B L, L as in Lima, seven seven zero, four eight three.
CM: B L seven seven zero four eight three.
DME: Correct. Once the prescription is in we can overnight it. Is she still at twenty-six oh one Marigold Lane, apartment three B?
MEMBER: Yes, but please don't leave it on the step, the box got stolen last time. Can you make it signature required?
DME: I'll flag signature required. So that's the three hundred unit cartridges, a ten-pack, and the twenty-three inch tubing sets.
CM: And just so you have it for quantity, she runs about forty-five units a day total, basal plus boluses.
MEMBER: Can you email me the tracking? It's priya dot raman ninety-one at example dot net.
DME: Priya dot raman nine one... at example dot net. Got it. I'll leave it pending prescription and you'll get an email when it ships.

CM: Cadence care management, this is Ines, how can I help?
MEMBER: Yeah hi, it's Walter Delacroix, uh, D E L A C R O I X, you all helped me get the power chair last year.
CM: Hi Mister Delacroix. Yes I see you. What's going on with the chair?
MEMBER: The joystick, it just quit on me Saturday night. Lights come on, won't go. I've been stuck in the recliner, my son's had to—
SON: Dad, let me, let me talk to her. Hi, this is Andre, his son.
CM: Hi Andre. Mister Delacroix, you're okay with me talking with him?
MEMBER: Yeah, yeah, go ahead.
SON: So we called the vendor, Ridgeway Mobility, and they said the earliest tech is a week from Thursday. He can't wait that long. He's got MS, he's seventy-three, he's two hundred forty pounds, I can't keep lifting him.
CM: Understood. Did they give you a work order number?
SON: Uh, R W dash, one one eight, wait, one one nine four six.
CM: R W one one nine four six. Okay. I'm going to call their service manager and push for an expedited visit, and in the meantime I'll see about a loaner manual chair.
SON: That'd help a lot. Tell them to come to the house, it's Rural Route four, box ninety-one, out past the Dollar General on seventeen, in Harlan.
CM: Rural Route four, box ninety-one. And the best number to reach you?
SON: Mine, six oh six, five five five, zero one three eight. His landline's dead half the time.
CM: Got it. Just to verify for the vendor, his member ID?
MEMBER: I got it right here. nine nine oh four, two two one, eight seven.
CM: Thank you. I'll call you back within a couple hours either way.
SON: Thanks Ines.

CM: Hi, is this Keisha? It's Dolores from Cadence, returning your call.
MEMBER: Yes, hi, thank you for calling back, I'm kind of freaking out.
CM: Take your time. What happened?
MEMBER: So the landlord taped a notice on my door Monday, it says I've got fourteen days or they file. I'm behind two months because I was out after the fistula surgery and Harmon Logistics never paid the short-term disability like they said they would.
CM: Okay. That's a lot to deal with. First, are you still on Wexford Terrace?
MEMBER: Yeah, fourteen ten Wexford Terrace, unit two oh seven.
CM: Two oh seven, right. Does the notice have a case number or anything?
MEMBER: No, it just says notice to pay or quit. Nothing's been filed yet I don't think.
CM: Good, that gives us some room. I'm going to refer you to the emergency rental assistance program through Tri-County Community Action, and there's a free legal aid clinic, they do walk-ins on Wednesdays at the library.
MEMBER: Wednesdays I can do. Dialysis is Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday.
CM: Perfect. For the application they'll want proof of income, the notice, and your lease. Do you have an email so I can send you the form?
MEMBER: It's k underscore bellamy at example dot org. Bellamy, B E L L A M Y.
CM: Got it. And date of birth for the referral?
MEMBER: June third, eighty-four.
CM: Okay, Miss Bellamy, I'm sending the referral now. Also, do you want me to talk to your social worker at the unit about the disability paperwork?
MEMBER: Please. Her name's Ayesha, she's there on dialysis days.
CM: I'll reach out to her. You did the right thing calling.
MEMBER: Thank you so much, Dolores.

CM: Hi, I need to book an in-person interpreter. This is Paul Wen with Cadence.
AGENCY: Sure, Yvette here at Bridgeword Language Services. What language?
CM: Haitian Creole. It's for a member, last name Jean-Baptiste, first name Marie-Claude.
AGENCY: Can you spell the last name for me?
CM: J E A N, hyphen, B A P T I S T E.
AGENCY: Okay. And the appointment?
CM: It's a cardiology follow-up at Lakeview Heart and Vascular, three thirty North Halsted, suite four hundred. With doctor Sorensen. October twenty-third at nine forty-five.
AGENCY: Twenty-third, nine forty-five. How long should I book?
CM: Ninety minutes, they're doing an echo too. She's seventy-nine, she's got A fib, they're adjusting her Eliquis. And, um, she prefers a female interpreter if that's possible.
AGENCY: We have Fabienne that morning, she does a lot of medical. Do you have a member ID for billing?
CM: Yes, it's M C, zero zero four, five five, nine one, two, sorry, scratch that, nine one three.
AGENCY: So M C zero zero four five five nine one three.
CM: That's it.
AGENCY: And a contact for day-of, in case she's running late?
CM: Her son Wesner usually brings her. His cell is seven seven three, five five five, zero one nine one. Please make sure the clinic doesn't just use him to interpret, she's asked for a professional.
AGENCY: Noted, I'll put that in the job notes. Your confirmation number is B W, two six eight eight one.
CM: B W two six eight eight one. Thank you, Yvette.

SCHOOL_NURSE: Hi, this is Gail Herrington, I'm the nurse over at Pinecrest Elementary. I'm calling about a student, Mateo Villanueva, his mom signed a release for us to talk with his care manager.
CM: Yes, hi, I'm Hannah, I have Mateo. What's going on?
SCHOOL_NURSE: So a couple things. The inhaler we keep here expired, and he's had three episodes in the last two weeks. Yesterday he needed the albuterol twice before lunch, two puffs each time.
CM: Oh, that's not good. Can you confirm his date of birth for me?
SCHOOL_NURSE: February fourteenth, twenty seventeen. Valentine's baby.
CM: Yep, that's him. And do you have a Medicaid number on your form?
SCHOOL_NURSE: I only have the last four, it's two eight eight one.
CM: That matches. Has mom been able to get him in to doctor Mbeki?
SCHOOL_NURSE: That's the thing, Lucia, his mom, works nights at the Tyson plant and she's been having a hard time. She said the clinic only does mornings.
CM: Okay. I can help with that, there's a pediatric clinic with Saturday hours. What number do you have for her?
SCHOOL_NURSE: The one on our emergency card is four seven nine, five five five, zero one zero four.
CM: Hm, that's different from ours, ours ends in, um, oh one five two. I'll try both.
SCHOOL_NURSE: Also, he has PE on Tuesdays and Fridays and the gym teacher wants a note about pre-treating before exercise.
CM: Makes sense. I'll ask the doctor for an updated asthma action plan and a new school inhaler. Where should I send it?
SCHOOL_NURSE: You can email me, g herrington at example dot org, that's g, h, e, double r, i, n, g, t, o, n.
CM: Got it. Thank you for calling, this is really helpful.

CM: Hello, this is Bridget calling from Cadence. I'm looking for Sunita?
NIECE: Speaking. Is this about my uncle?
CM: Yes, about Mister Kapoor. I got your voicemail that the guardianship went through.
NIECE: It did, finally. The judge signed the letters of guardianship on September eighteenth. It took almost five months.
CM: Congratulations, I know that's been a long road. To update his file I'll need a copy of the letters. Can you read me the case number?
NIECE: Sure, it's, um, two five, G A, zero zero three one seven, from Franklin County Probate Court.
CM: Two five G A zero zero three one seven. And just to verify I have the right member, his date of birth?
NIECE: March second, nineteen forty-five. He's eighty-one.
CM: Thank you. And he's still at Willow Bend?
NIECE: Yes, Willow Bend Memory Care, on the second floor now. They moved him after the fall last month. His resident number there is W B, four four zero two, if you need it.
CM: That's helpful. And for our records, how do you spell your full name?
NIECE: Sunita, S U N I T A, and the last name is Kapoor-Hayes, with a hyphen. K A P O O R, hyphen, H A Y E S.
CM: And where should I email the authorization form?
NIECE: sunita dot k h at example dot com.
CM: Okay. Once that's signed, you'll be the decision-maker on file. I'll also let doctor Petrakis know, since she does his memory care visits.
NIECE: Good. His Alzheimer's has gotten a lot worse, he's on the Namenda and the donepezil, and honestly I don't know if they're doing anything anymore.
CM: That's a good question for the next care conference. They do those every ninety days.
NIECE: Okay. Thank you, Bridget.

OFFICE: Rheumatology, this is Kenji.
CM: Hi Kenji, it's Shauna from Cadence care management. I'm calling about Gloria Esposito, the denial on her biologic.
OFFICE: Oh yes, Mrs. Esposito. Hold on, let me pull her up. Date of birth?
CM: Eight, nineteen, fifty-eight.
OFFICE: Okay. Yeah, we got the denial letter, it's dated September twenty-ninth. They're saying step therapy wasn't documented.
CM: But she was on methotrexate for, what, eighteen months? And she had the liver enzymes go up.
OFFICE: Right, and then sulfasalazine, she couldn't tolerate it. It's all in the chart, it just didn't get attached. Doctor Abboud wants to do a peer-to-peer and a written appeal.
CM: Great. We have sixty days from the letter, so we're fine on time. Can you give me the reference number from the denial?
OFFICE: It's P A two six, dash, seven seven three one zero.
CM: P A two six seven seven three one zero. And what member ID did you submit under? I want to make sure it's not the old one.
OFFICE: R, X, four oh one, D as in David, eight eight five.
CM: Was that a B or a D?
OFFICE: D as in David.
CM: Okay, that's current. And I'll need doctor Abboud's NPI for the appeal form.
OFFICE: one four eight two, six six zero, three nine one.
CM: One four eight two six six zero three nine one. Perfect. Her CRP last time was twenty-four and she said her hands are so swollen she can't open jars.
OFFICE: Yeah, she was in tears at the last visit. We'll send the letter of medical necessity by Wednesday.
CM: Thank you. Can you cc me? s dot oduya at example dot com.
OFFICE: Got it.

DRIVER: Yeah, hi, I'm the driver from Clearbreath Home Medical, I got a delivery for a, uh, Eldon Yoder, and the GPS has me in the middle of a cornfield.
CM: Oh no. Okay, this is Trevor at Cadence, I'm his care manager. What address do you have?
DRIVER: Seventeen County Road two twelve, Millersburg.
CM: That's right. Let me get his wife on the line, hold on... Ruth? Hi, it's Trevor from Cadence, I've got the oxygen driver here, he can't find the house.
WIFE: Oh for heaven's sake, they always do that. Where is he?
DRIVER: I'm by a red barn, there's a hand-painted sign for brown eggs.
WIFE: Okay, you went too far. Turn around, go back about a mile, and we're the white house with the green roof, right across from the Salt Creek Mennonite church. Mailbox says Yoder, but half the road says Yoder, so look for the church.
DRIVER: Got it, church, white house, green roof.
CM: While I have you, can you confirm the order? I want to make sure it's the right setup.
DRIVER: Order number C B, three three oh, seven one six. Five liter concentrator, twelve E tanks, a conserving regulator, and fifty feet of tubing.
WIFE: Fifty feet? He's on two liters continuous, the doctor said, and he sleeps upstairs.
CM: That's right, two liters per minute, and up to three with exertion. Fifty feet should get him from the bedroom to the bathroom.
WIFE: Well, the last company only brought twenty-five and he kept pulling it off the nightstand.
DRIVER: I'll show him how to do the tank swap too. Is he home all day?
WIFE: He's not going anywhere, honey. He's ninety-one.
CM: Ruth, the respiratory therapist from Clearbreath will call to set up a visit, probably early next week. Is the house phone still the best number?
WIFE: Yes, three three oh, five five five, zero one two nine. We don't do cell phones.
CM: Perfect. Driver, you're good?
DRIVER: Turning around now.

RN: Hi, this is Corinne, I'm a nurse with Cadence. May I speak with Tomasz Wisniewski?
MEMBER: That's me, but everybody calls me Tom. You got my labs?
RN: I do. Before I go over them, can you verify your date of birth and address?
MEMBER: January twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty. And it's fifty-five Orchard Hill Drive.
RN: Thank you, Tom. So these are from the draw at Harborview Lab on the twenty-ninth. Your A1c came back at nine point two.
MEMBER: Nine point two? It was eight something in the spring.
RN: It was eight point one in April, yeah. So it's gone up. Have you been taking the metformin?
MEMBER: Mostly. I, um, I ran out for a week or so when the pharmacy messed up the refill.
RN: Okay, that happens. The other thing is your potassium was five point six, which is a little high, and doctor Oyelaran wants to repeat it to make sure it wasn't a bad sample.
MEMBER: Is that dangerous?
RN: Mildly elevated. She wants it rechecked within a few days, and she said hold off on the salt substitute if you're using one, those are mostly potassium.
MEMBER: My wife bought the no-salt stuff! Bozena, hey, it's the potassium salt.
RN: That could definitely be part of it. Can you get to the lab Wednesday the eighth? They're open seven to three.
MEMBER: Wednesday's fine. Do I need a new order?
RN: It's already in. Just bring your ID and give them your medical record number, it's H V, zero zero six, two two four, seven nine.
MEMBER: Hold on, writing. H V... was it two two four seven nine?
RN: Zero zero six, then two two four, then seven nine.
MEMBER: Got it. And can you text me a reminder? My cell is two oh seven, five five five, zero one five nine.
RN: I'll set that up. And, Tom, your last name, is it W I S N I E W S K I? I want the text to have it right.
MEMBER: Perfect, most people forget the second W.

SW: Hi, this is Colleen Matsuda, I'm the social worker at Riverside Kidney Center. I'm trying to reach the care manager for Darnell Hutchins.
CM: That's me, Ravi. Is Darnell okay?
SW: Well, that's why I'm calling. He missed Tuesday and Thursday this week. He's normally very consistent, Tuesday Thursday Saturday, first shift.
CM: Oh, that's not like him at all. Did anybody reach him?
SW: I finally got him last night. He said his ride never came. Both days. He's with MedRide through the plan.
CM: Ugh. Okay. Did he say anything about how he's feeling?
SW: He's short of breath, his ankles are swollen, and his weight's probably up. He was already running about three kilos over his dry weight last Saturday... sorry, not last Saturday, the Saturday before. And his potassium was borderline.
CM: Should he be going to the ER?
SW: Our nephrologist, doctor Castellanos, wants him in for an extra treatment today if we can get him here by noon. Otherwise, yes, the ER.
CM: Okay, I'll set up a direct ride, not through the broker. He's still at the corner of Fifth and Linden, right? The building with the laundromat?
SW: That's what we have. Two forty Linden Avenue, Elizabeth.
CM: And you have a good number for him?
SW: His cell's been cutting out. His girlfriend Tasha picked up the second time, her number is nine oh eight, five five five, zero one eight seven.
CM: Nine oh eight, five five five, oh one eight seven. Okay. Let me get the ride booked and I'll call you right back with a pickup time.
SW: Thank you. Our chair opens at eleven thirty.

CM: Hi Linda, it's Joel from Cadence. I'm just checking in on you and Frank.
CAREGIVER: Oh. Hi. Sorry, I, I was just sitting down. It's been a day.
CM: That's okay. How are things?
CAREGIVER: Honestly? Not good. He fell again last Sunday, in the bathroom, and I couldn't get him up. I had to call the fire department to come lift him. And he was up all night Tuesday, the hallucinations, he thought there were kids in the yard.
CM: That sounds really exhausting. Are you getting any sleep?
CAREGIVER: Maybe four hours. And I still have my shifts at Giant Eagle, three mornings a week, because we need the money. I'm, I'm seventy-two years old. I can't...
CM: Take your time.
CAREGIVER: Sorry. My sister Margit keeps telling me to put him in a home, but she's in Cleveland, she doesn't see it.
CM: Linda, what you're describing is caregiver burnout, and it's really common with Parkinson's. You don't have to choose between doing everything and a nursing home. Is he still going to Sunrise Adult Day?
CAREGIVER: Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, yes. That's the only time I breathe.
CM: Okay. I'd like to refer you to Lake Erie Area Agency on Aging for in-home respite, they can send an aide for a few hours or do a short overnight stay somewhere. And there's a caregiver support group on Thursday evenings.
CAREGIVER: I don't know if I can do a group.
CM: That's fine, no pressure. Also, the hallucinations, I want to let doctor Haddad know, sometimes the carbidopa levodopa timing or another med can cause that.
CAREGIVER: Okay. Yes. Please. Oh, and our fiftieth anniversary is the nineteenth, I, I just want him to be home for that.
CM: Then let's make that the goal. I'll call you back with the respite intake info. Is this home number still best?
CAREGIVER: Yes, four four zero, five five five, zero one four one.

CM: Mister Whitfield, it's Alana with Cadence. Is this a good time?
MEMBER: Good as any. Call me Clarence.
CM: Okay, Clarence. Last time you mentioned you served, and I wanted to follow up about VA benefits, specifically Aid and Attendance, that could help pay for an aide.
MEMBER: Yeah. Army, sixty-nine to seventy-one. Vietnam. I never did anything with the VA though, my wife always said we didn't need it.
CM: Well, with the diabetes and the neuropathy there may be a presumptive connection, because of Agent Orange. Do you have your DD two fourteen?
MEMBER: Somewhere. My daughter Renee has a box of papers, she lives out in Arizona now.
CM: That's okay, the veterans service officer can request it. I'd like to connect you with Ramon Escobedo, he's at the Marion County Veterans Service Office. They do this for free.
MEMBER: Ramon. Okay.
CM: Do you remember your service number, or did they use your social?
MEMBER: Back then it was a service number. I know this one by heart, R A, five four, one one six, two zero eight.
CM: R A five four one one six two zero eight. I'll pass that along. Have you ever been seen at the Halstead VA clinic?
MEMBER: Once, maybe two summers ago, for a hearing test. They gave me hearing aids I never wear.
CM: Clarence! Okay, we'll talk about that another time. Ramon will want to meet in person. He does home visits on Fridays. Would Friday the seventeenth work?
MEMBER: I don't go anywhere. Sure.
CM: And you're still on Tecumseh Street, the house by the old Shell station?
MEMBER: Four oh nine Tecumseh. Tell him the doorbell don't work, knock loud.
CM: Ha, I will. He'll call you first from his office line. You're seventy-five, right? I just want to note it on the referral.
MEMBER: Seventy-six in December.
CM: Got it. I'll send the referral today and call you after he reaches out.

PHARMACY: Thank you for calling CareDirect Mail Pharmacy, my name is Devon, who am I speaking with?
MEMBER: This is Rosalind Tafoya, and I've got my care manager on with me.
CM: Hi, Esperanza from Cadence.
PHARMACY: Hi both. Ms. Tafoya, can I get your date of birth and zip code?
MEMBER: May fifth, nineteen fifty-two, and zip is eight eight oh six one.
PHARMACY: Thank you. How can I help?
MEMBER: Well, my packages keep getting left at the road and the heat ruins them. I got a P O box now. I want everything sent there.
PHARMACY: Sure. Go ahead with the box.
MEMBER: P O Box four eighty-eight, Silver City, New Mexico, same zip.
PHARMACY: P O Box four eight eight. Okay, updated. Anything else?
CM: Yes, her metoprolol. She takes twenty-five milligrams, half a tab twice a day, but the last shipment only had thirty tablets, which is a month, not ninety days.
PHARMACY: Let me look. Prescription number?
MEMBER: It's on the bottle... seven oh, two two, nine, one four, six.
PHARMACY: Hmm, I'm not finding that. Can you read it again?
MEMBER: Seven oh two two nine one four... six. Oh wait, no, that's a three at the end, my glasses. Seven oh two two nine one four three.
PHARMACY: There it is. Yeah, it was entered as thirty days. I'll need a new script from the prescriber for the ninety-day.
CM: That's doctor Benally at Gila Family Health. I'll call them.
PHARMACY: Perfect. Her Eliquis and atorvastatin are scheduled to ship October fourteenth, so if we get the metoprolol by then we'll bundle them.
MEMBER: And to the P O box.
PHARMACY: To the P O box, yes ma'am.

MEMBER: Hello? Is this, um, Cadence? I need to talk to Miss Okonjo.
CM: This is Adaeze Okonjo, hi. Who am I speaking with?
MEMBER: It's Hector, Hector Ruiz. My English is not so good, sorry, I'm better in Spanish.
CM: That's okay, Mister Ruiz, I can get an interpreter if you want, or we can try in English first.
MEMBER: English is okay. Slow. I have bedbugs. In the bed, in the couch, everywhere. Three weeks now.
CM: Oh no. Are you getting bites?
MEMBER: Yes, my arms, my back. Very bad. I scratch at night, and with my sugar, the diabetes, I am afraid of infection.
CM: You're right to worry about that. Any redness spreading, warm, pus?
MEMBER: One on the leg is red. Big.
CM: Okay, I want you to have that looked at. I'll call Brockton Neighborhood Health to see if they can see you tomorrow. Have you told the building?
MEMBER: I tell the office two times... no... I tell them September fifteen and again last week. They say they will spray. Nobody comes.
CM: Okay. Let's file a complaint with the Brockton Housing Authority. You're still at eight hundred Pruitt Avenue?
MEMBER: Yes, apartment, um, eleven C. Eleven, C like cat.
CM: Eleven C. And a phone number they can call?
MEMBER: Five oh eight, five five five, zero one one seven. Or my daughter, Marisol, she speaks English good.
CM: What's her number?
MEMBER: Five oh eight, five five five, zero one... six six.
CM: Okay. I'm filing it online right now. They gave me a complaint number, H C, two six, zero four, four one. I'll text it to you.
MEMBER: Thank you. And for the bites, can I use Benadryl?
CM: The cream or a tablet at night is usually okay, but let the doctor look at the leg first. I'll call you back with the appointment.

SCHEDULER: Hi, this is Lorena calling from Amberfield Home Health. I'm trying to reach the family of Opal Abernathy?
DAUGHTER: This is her daughter, Celeste. Is this about the wound nurse?
SCHEDULER: Yes! We got the referral from Cadence and from doctor Whitaker's office. It looks like she has a stage three pressure injury on the sacrum and she'll need a wound vac.
DAUGHTER: Yes, they put the vac on at the hospital before she left. She came home Saturday.
SCHEDULER: Okay. So the wound nurse would come out three times a week, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, for dressing changes. For the start of care, our nurse Kateryna can come Tuesday the fourteenth, late morning?
DAUGHTER: Tuesday the... wait, isn't that too long? The hospital said someone would come within forty-eight hours.
SCHEDULER: Sorry, you're right, I'm looking at the wrong week. Let me... tomorrow, Tuesday, eleven o'clock.
DAUGHTER: Okay, tomorrow at eleven. I'll be there, I'm taking off work.
SCHEDULER: Great. Can I confirm the address? I have two twenty-nine Bramble Ridge Lane.
DAUGHTER: That's right. It's a gated community, the gate code is four four one seven pound.
SCHEDULER: Four four one seven pound. And her date of birth?
DAUGHTER: The thirtieth of July, nineteen forty.
SCHEDULER: And the Medicare or plan ID, just to verify eligibility?
DAUGHTER: I have the Cadence card, it's A B, nine three, oh oh seven, five two, hold on, the last digit might be an eight, it's smudged.
SCHEDULER: No problem, I'll verify with the plan. And your number?
DAUGHTER: Eight six five, five five five, zero one two two.
SCHEDULER: Perfect. And Mrs. Abernathy is she on any blood thinners?
DAUGHTER: Aspirin eighty-one, that's it. And she's diabetic, A1c was seven something.
SCHEDULER: Okay, thank you, Celeste. Kateryna will call about thirty minutes before.

CM: Hi, is this Mrs. Fenwick?
MEMBER: Mrs. who?
CM: Fenwick. Beatrice Fenwick?
MEMBER: Oh, yes, yes, that's me, sorry, I don't have my hearing aids in. Who's calling?
CM: It's Nadia, from Cadence, your care manager.
MEMBER: Lydia?
CM: Nadia. N, like Nancy. That's alright. I'm calling to remind you about your memory check appointment.
MEMBER: My what? Hold on, let me give you to Lloyd. Lloyd! It's the insurance.
